title: orobanche arenaria f. robusta
intro: Orobanche arenaria f. robusta, commonly known as the sand broom or sand holoparasite, is a species of broomrape that is a parasitic plant that derives its nutrients by connecting to the roots of host plants. This plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health issues, including fever, inflammation, and respiratory problems, due to its health benefits such as antioxidant, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory properties. The therapeutic actions of Orobanche arenaria f. robusta include analgesic, anti-pyretic, and anti-inflammatory effects, making it a potential treatment for conditions like arthritis and other inflammatory diseases. The bioactive constituents of this plant include alkaloids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic properties.
